citations.narrative:
While inspecting the outside cage wash room, APHIS Officials observed multiple holes in the aluminum ceiling
approximately 3-6 inches in the center of the ceiling where sunlight was coming through. Officials also observed too
numerous to count holes approximately 0.5 inch to 2 inches in diameter throughout the ceiling. The supporting beam was
also severely rusted. The holes in the ceiling have gotten bigger since the last routine inspection on July 22, 2025. The
holes on the roof are big enough where pests have an entrance point and have access to animals, equipment, and rooms.
Housing facilities for non-human primates must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound for the
species of non-human primates housed in them. They must be kept in good repair, and they must protect the animals
from injury, contain the animals securely, and restrict other animals from entering.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with Facility Representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Lemnique Wafer, Assistant Director n
